# Reviewed false positives for the content secret scan in
# .github/workflows/flutter_ci.yml (secret-guard job).
#
# One `path:line` per line, repository-relative, matched as a whole line.
#
# Adding an entry means a reviewer looked at that exact line and agreed it is
# not a credential. The reason belongs in the pull request that adds it. If the
# line moves, the entry stops matching and the finding comes back, which is the
# intended behaviour: an allowlist should not outlive the thing it excused.
#
# If a real secret is ever found, do NOT allowlist it and do NOT simply delete
# the line. Rotate the credential first; the value is already in git history and
# in anyone's clone. See SECURITY.md.
#

# HIT-009: Firebase client API keys, one per platform, in the files the
# FlutterFire CLI generates for the hitup-691be project. They identify the
# project to Firebase and are compiled into every copy of the app, so they are
# not secrets; SECURITY.md ("Firebase client config vs admin secrets") says so.
# Access is enforced by Firestore security rules, not by keeping these hidden.
# Regenerating the files can move these lines; re-review them when it does.

ios/Runner/GoogleService-Info.plist:6
lib/firebase_options.dart:53
lib/firebase_options.dart:61
